{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABdSkaSg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGzZOA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 144, "title": "Profile and optimize Rust/Wasm performance with free PC-98 games kept outside Git", "body": "## Problem

After #140 (V30/i486 instruction-cycle timing) and #142 (dedicated render Worker), a target PC-98 DOS game reportedly runs **much more slowly and its music playback has become worse**. Existing synthetic/rights-cleared fixture and CI passes do not prove that real games run at the required rate on ordinary browser hardware. We need to measure **actual game workloads**, find the dominant host-side costs, and implement evidence-based optimizations—not change emulated CPU clocks or merely add buffers to conceal sustained underproduction.

This task is distinct from #13 (compatibility discovery), #138 (sound correctness/continuity), #140 (guest CPU timing) and #142 (render Worker architecture): it requires **real-game performance profiling and delivered optimizations with before/after evidence**.

## Goal

Use legitimately obtainable **free PC-98/PC-9821 DOS games or playable demos** as local performance workloads to profile and optimize the Rust/Wasm runtime. The test *game software/media are never committed to Git* and must not enter published assets, CI uploads, PR attachments or logs.

In PC-98 contexts these are usually **floppy/HDD disk images, DOS executables and game assets**, not firmware ROMs. Do not require proprietary BIOS ROMs or commercial game files.

### License and local-only media policy (required)

- Prefer games distributed by their original author/publisher for permitted local download/play and testing; inspect each game's actual terms, including included art/audio/drivers. **Freeware/free download/abandonware does not automatically grant redistribution.** Keeping media out of Git substantially reduces distribution exposure but **does not remove licensing, downloading, execution or sharing obligations**.
- Start with the previously audited, MIT-licensed [ADV98](https://github.com/yarufu/pc98) plus original, rights-cleared PMD music, then obtain at least one additional legally available game/demo **if needed** to exercise slower image transitions, sustained FM/SSG BGM, HDD I/O and/or CPU-heavy loops. If no suitable additional title is lawful/available, explicitly document the limitation and use existing rights-cleared workloads; do not fetch unauthorized mirrors or bypass protection.
- Store downloaded archives, extracted game assets, disk/HDI/FD images, generated saves, audio captures and full screenshots **only outside the Git working tree** (preferred) or under verified `.gitignore`d local test directories. Confirm with `git check-ignore`, `git status --short` and publishing/asset audits. Do not upload raw files to hosted CI, issue/PR comments, GitHub releases, Pages, chats or benchmark artifacts.
- A small **text-only** manifest/runbook may be committed with game name/version, official source URL, checksum, license/use notes, local acquisition instructions, and repeatable scenario; no bundled bytes or copyrighted media. Avoid automatic hosted-CI downloads of local-only titles. Leave current explicitly licensed CI fixtures untouched.
- Prefer local-only execution without collecting or disclosing private/copyrighted media. Benchmark reports should contain derived numeric metrics and self-authored observations, **not** disassembly dumps, substantial game logs, soundtrack audio or captured game frames.

## Investigation and optimization

1. **Establish reproducible, representative game workloads.** Pin source/version and SHA-256 when permitted; record guest machine profile (VM V30-10 or Ap DX2-66), boot configuration, scene sequence, BGM state and media access, browser/OS/host hardware, Wasm/build revision, and precise measurement windows. Use at least one scene transition with music and one CPU/VRAM- or HDD-intensive segment. Run the same deterministic steps on the same build/hardware.
2. **Measure baseline with the real production release-Wasm browser path**, including Chromium and Firefox where available; compare normal render Worker with the existing `?diagnostics&renderer=inline` path. Record guest seconds/wall second, completed instructions/second, CPU cycles, guest-slice wall time and p95/p99, display fps/presentation latency/frame coalescing, HDD reads, PCM produced vs consumed, underrun samples, overflow/drops, queue depth and BGM tempo/pitch/IRQ cadence. Distinguish an emulator running slower than real time from an intentionally slow *guest* workload.
3. **Profile actual bottlenecks**, first in Rust/Wasm CPU decode/dispatch and instruction timing/accounting, RAM/VRAM address translation, transaction/rollback and cache simulation; also profile FM/SSG/PCM synthesis, PIT/IRQ/device ticking, memory copies/snapshots, rasterization and Worker scheduling. Attribute CPU-hot functions via host profiler where feasible; do not presume the render Worker is the cause.
4. **Implement high-impact host-side optimizations** guided by evidence: eliminate repeated calculations/allocations/clones, specialize hot paths, reduce redundant memory translation/validation, optimize device/audio sampling without changing register/timer semantics, and reduce unnecessary frame/VRAM copying. Evaluate build-level Wasm improvements and Worker tuning only with A/B metrics. Avoid speculative refactors and new threads unless a proven net benefit outweighs sync/copy costs.
5. **Preserve guest correctness and real-time audio.** Keep the documented 10 MHz V30 and 66 MHz DX2 models, instruction cycles, 8 MHz device scheduler conversion, PIT/IRQ/FM/SSG/PCM phase, disk contents and graphics output. Do **not** fix performance by lowering virtual clocks, skipping guest instructions, speeding up/slowing down music, silently dropping work or growing audio latency indefinitely. Test pause/resume, reset, mute/unmute, scene changes and both render paths.
6. **Validate each optimization before merging.** Repeat baseline scenarios on exactly controlled hardware/builds; report actual before/after results (including negative results) for emulated-time throughput, scene transition wall time, audio missing samples, render fps, host CPU and memory. Maintain existing native, browser, packaging/security/licensing tests and add small original/test-licensed synthetic regressions for optimization invariants that CI can legally run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one legal, playable PC-98 game/demo is **actually executed locally** as a non-Git benchmark; source/use rights, version, hash, setup and scenario are documented. Prefer at least two distinct workload types when available.
- [ ] Identify and quantify the principal performance bottleneck(s) in the **real-game** trace, separating insufficient PCM production, scheduling/queue jitter, guest-clock modeling, video rendering and media load/decompression.
- [ ] Deliver at least one measurable, justified **runtime optimization** targeted at the observed bottleneck (or report concrete failed attempts/blockers without claiming the issue completed).
- [ ] Provide reproducible numeric before/after measurements on identical guest scenarios and host conditions, clearly marking results that remain below 1.0 guest second per wall second or still underrun. Do not claim an all-game fix from a single demo.
- [ ] Existing CPU timing, device/IRQ, sound pitch/tempo, graphics/disk and browser regression contracts still hold; no unlicensed media are added to tracked files, publication directories, CI artifacts or uploaded test results.

## Related work

- #13 — local-only real-game compatibility testing; reuse the media-safety policy.
- #138 — licensed ADV98/FM music playback investigation.
- #140 — V30/i486 cycle timing accuracy (preserve guest cycles).
- #142 — render-Worker work; verify whether it benefits or harms each workload.

**Scope:** profile and optimize *host execution cost* while retaining the chosen emulated hardware's cycle/timing behavior.
